title: Šidák correction as a named independent-FWER cousin
dek: 1−(1−α)^{1/m} per test. Wikipedia independence recipe. Slightly sharper than Bonferroni when independence is real.
story: Šidák on Wikipedia is the exact FWER recipe if tests are independent: P(all true nulls kept) = (1−α')^m, so α' = 1−(1−α)^{1/m}. For small α/m it is almost Bonferroni.
LD and shared isolates violate independence. Then Šidák's exactness evaporates and you are back to 'maybe Bonferroni's union bound is the honest conservative thing, or permute'.
This card exists so a methods sentence that says Šidák is a named choice, not a mysterious SAS checkbox.
deep: For α=0.05, m=100, Bonferroni 0.0005; Šidák ≈ 0.000513. The gain is tiny; the assumption is not.
Positive dependence usually makes FWER smaller than the independent calculation — but do not bet a paper on that vibe.
Holm can use Šidák steps too (Holm–Šidák).
GWAS 5e-8 is not Šidák of 0.05 on 1e6 exactly in every paper; it is a convention.

visual.caption: Tiny gap between Bonferroni and Šidák thresholds versus a large gap if you refuse the independence story (schematic).
